issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with two parameters (int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput), but the problem statement's specification and the solution implementation define addGuestStudents(int) with a single int parameter. This mismatch in the method signature is structural and will confuse students about the required method to implement and may cause compilation/test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature to match the specification and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). If input validation is desired, implement it internally or provide an overloaded private helper method; do not require an extra boolean parameter in the public API so it aligns with the UML/problem description and the solution.

issues.description: The template's Lecture.addGuestStudents method signature includes an extra boolean parameter (addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput)) while both the problem statement and the solution expect a single-parameter method addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch of the same conceptual operation (adding guest students) across artifacts can confuse students about which signature to implement and may cause compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template method signature with the problem statement and solution by changing the template declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } If input validation is required, perform it inside this single-parameter method or provide an overload that delegates to an internal validation helper, but do not change the publicly required signature.
